the shear viscosity of QCD at vanishing chemical potential is of order 10-4 times the shear viscosity of water, that the shear viscosity is a monotonically increasing function of temperature, and that the ratio of the bulk viscosity to the shear viscosity is small and negative at vanishing chemical potentials and temperatures above 100 MeV.

the viscosity of QED and QCD matter is low, but not zero.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the viscosity of strongly interacting matter at high temperature is small but non-zero and the shear viscosity to entropy density ratio η/s is close to its conjectured lower bound of 1/4π.
we are able to provide a first measurement of the shear viscosity of the QGP.

we have shown that the viscosity of a QCD plasma is not a number, but rather depends on the temperature, the baryon chemical potential and the coupling strength, which is a function of both the temperature and the chemical potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shear viscosity of the QCD plasma is small, but not as small as previously thought.
the viscosity-to-entropy ratio of QCD matter is very small, of the order 0.1.
the viscosity of QED matter is much lower than that of QCD matter, and that it is possible to extract the shear viscosity of the latter by measuring the elliptic flow of the former.
